messages:
deploy-bot: ALERT: Canary failure detected for model rollout v2.3.4 -> v2.4.0 in us-east-1. error_rate spike 12min ago. metric: generation_errors_per_1k = 28 (baseline 2). tagging thread for on-call and infra. <https://internal.metrics/redwood/canary/2.4.0|canary dashboard>
incident-bot: Paging on-call: @Priya K (ml-oncall) and @Marcus L (sre-oncall). Severity: P1 - customer visible errors for subset of traffic. See incident playbook: #incidents/runbooks/model-rollout
Priya K: reading the dashboard. I see error pattern on streaming responses: connection resets + malformed-json from runtime. sample error: `runtime: kv-cache miss -> invalid tokenization chunk` — weird. Assigning to Sasha for runtime kernel checks. Marcus, can you confirm if infra network flaps or pod restarts? 
Marcus L: checking k8s: no node restarts in the last hour. pod restarts: 3 in the canary pool (gpux-2.4.0-canary-*) starting 2004002950 -> 2004003055. Logs show OOM-kill on one pod then liveness loops. Pulling logs now. 
Sasha R: looking at runtime logs for v2.4.0. Not seeing OOM reasons; see repeated "failed to allocate KV cache segment" followed by immediate decoder exception: `json decode error at chunk boundary`. Suspect KV cache layout changed with quantization tweak in v2.4.0 build. Repro locally with small prompt? Trying now. 
Diego: Customer impact: Support reports 6 customers in last 20m with generation failures (error 502/invalid-response). No billing anomalies. Customers are on dedicated and hosted routing — looks concentrated in us-east-1 canary traffic only so far. 
Priya K: good, scope is canary. Key Q: does v2.4.0 differ in tokenizer or model spec? who built the release? Sasha, do we have commit/manifest? 
Sasha R: build metadata: v2.4.0 -> commit a7f9d3, changed: - int8 quant integration for attention kernels + small tokenizer fix. Diff snippet:
```
modelspec.json
- "tokenizer": "vocab_v1"
+ "tokenizer": "vocab_v1+patch"
runtime/config/kv_cache.py
- default_segment_size = 64MB
+ default_segment_size = 48MB
```
Marcus L: that matches OOM/kv failures. Smaller segment size + quantization -> more contiguous allocations. If segment too small we might fragment and fail allocation leading to partial output and decoder errors. Hypothesis: kv_cache segsize change caused allocation failures under certain seq lengths -> decoder state corrupted -> malformed JSON. 
Priya K: hypothesis noted. Next steps: 1) collect full canary logs + core dumps -> Sasha to upload, 2) run diffed canary workload replay against v2.3.4 and v2.4.0 to reproduce, 3) pin routing to v2.3.4 if customers continue to hit errors. Who can get the replay running? 
Sasha R: I'll run local replay and push logs to /shared/incidents/2004003001/logs. attaching samplereq that triggered fail: `{"prompt":"<user>...","max_tokens":512}`. 
Marcus L: I'll prepare a quick routing pin and rollback plan. For autopilot: we can update routing rule to pin canary tags to v2.3.4 and scale down canary nodes for v2.4.0. ETA ~10m for safe pin. Need explicit approval for rollback from ML on-call. 
Priya K: approve pin to v2.3.4. Do it. Keep canary isolated for debugging. Also open a tracking ticket: 0/impact to prod beyond canary -> but customers hit were canary routed, so rollforward for core prod not needed yet. 
Marcus L: doing `curl -XPOST https://api.internal/redwood/route/pin -d '{"canary_pool":"us-east-1:canary","model":"v2.3.4"}'` -> response: 202 accepted. routing change propagated. Monitoring now.
incident-bot: ROUTING_CHANGE: Pin applied by Marcus L at 2004003270. New canary traffic % -> 0%. 
Diego: customer page updates: Informing affected customers that we rolled back canary and investigating. No SLA hits expected yet. 
Sasha R: repro successful locally: with workload X (avg seq 380) v2.4.0 throws repeated `kv_cache allocation failed` after ~15 tokens; v2.3.4 runs fine. Core dump attached. Uploading to /shared/incidents/2004003001/artifacts/core-v2.4.0.gz
Priya K: good repro. Hypotheses prioritized: 1) kv_cache segment size reduction + quantization coupling -> allocation fragmentation (high likelihood), 2) tokenizer patch mismatch causing boundary corruption (medium), 3) regression in attention kernel (low). Let's run a targeted binary with restored segment size. Sasha, can you build v2.4.0 with default_segment_size=64MB and run replay? 
Sasha R: building patched v2.4.0+fix_kvseg now. Will run replay and post perf diff. 
Marcus L: note for RCA timeline: started at 2004003001 alert. Pager notify 2004003002. Pin applied 2004003270. Repro confirmed 2004003350. Starting to assemble timeline and hypothesis table in the incident ticket: https://tracker.internal/INC-2004003001
Priya K: handoff: I'm going offline for personal emergency at 2004003500; handing to Marcus. Marcus, you own the next steps: coordinate with QA for a backport patch test, and decide whether to roll v2.4.0 back globally after patch. Leave notes in ticket. :handshake:
oncall-handoff-bot: HANDOFF NOTICE: Priya K -> Marcus L at 2004003500. Pager duty escalations routed to Marcus.
Marcus L: acknowledged. I'll coordinate patch testing and schedule a postmortem once we confirm root cause. If patched build passes replay and stress tests, we'll re-enable canary with reduced parallelism and ramp metrics. If not, we'll mark v2.4.0 as "do not promote" and pin stable until next build. 
Sasha R: quick preliminary diff output (canary metrics):
- v2.3.4 generation_success_rate: 99.8%
- v2.4.0 generation_success_rate: 97.1 -> after pin 99.9 (residual traffic)
- latency p95 v2.4.0 slightly improved but not worth regressions. uploading full canary diff csv to /shared/incidents/2004003001/canary-diff.csv
Priya K: thanks. Summary for RCA thread: cause suspected kv_cache sizing + quantization interaction; mitigation = pin to v2.3.4; fix = revert segsize or adjust allocation logic + QA stress on seq-length distribution. Marcus, Sasha, open follow-up RFC for safer kv cache defaults and integrate canary tests that exercise long sequences. 
Marcus L: created follow-up RFC: RFC-2004003001 (kv-cache defaults + canary stress harness). Adding Sasha as owner. 
Diego: support notifying customers: "We rolled back canary traffic after observing an intermittent generation error affecting some preview traffic. No broader production impact. We'll follow up with RCA." 
Priya K: leaving final note: please capture exact core dump stack traces in the ticket and tag build owner (a7f9d3). Marcus, escalate to release manager if we need a hotfix. I'm out. 
Marcus L: will do. maintaining watch. Incident thread will be updated with postmortem. :white_check_mark:
